payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.

risks: The visible tests leave malformed graphs, missing predecessor keys, duplicate dependencies, self-cycles, multiple disconnected cycles, non-string keys, and locale-specific ordering unspecified; avoid inventing broad behavior beyond the existing object-of-arrays API and preserve ordinary lexicographic ordering.

If predecessor names are absent from graph keys, strict declared-predecessor containment will leave the node blocked; this is an unspecified edge case and should not prompt changes to the error contract.
Using a mutable or insertion-order-derived candidate collection could make wave or cycle ordering nondeterministic; all externally visible lists must derive from sorted node names.
unknowns: No visible test defines behavior for absent predecessor keys or malformed dependency values.
The research report does not include a successful checker run; Developer must provide the final node --test result after editing.

payload.objective: Implement dependencyWaves in src/waves.js so an object-shaped dependency graph yields deterministic lexicographically ordered execution waves: every node is scheduled only after all declared predecessors have appeared in earlier waves, and scheduling stalls raise the existing DependencyCycleError contract with only the sorted nodes still blocked.
acceptance_criteria: Return an array of waves, with each wave containing lexicographically sorted node names.
Sort graph nodes before every scheduling decision so object insertion order and dependency-array insertion order cannot affect output.
A node is eligible only when every declared predecessor is in the completed set from an earlier wave; do not place same-wave predecessors or fan-in dependents together.

If no unscheduled node is eligible, throw the existing DependencyCycleError with name DependencyCycleError, code DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes equal to the lexicographically sorted blocked nodes; independent nodes already scheduled must not appear in nodes.
Preserve the existing DependencyCycleError message and field behavior by constructing it with the sorted blocked list rather than replacing or reshaping the class.
Keep the change focused to src/waves.js; do not alter tests or package dependencies.
Run the real project checker node --test (via npm test if desired) and require all tests to pass.
payload.root_design_decision: Use a deterministic Kahn-style wave scheduler over the graph keys. Snapshot and lexicographically sort all node names once; maintain a completed set and unscheduled set; for each wave, filter the sorted unscheduled list to nodes whose declared predecessor list is fully contained in completed. Emit that already-sorted eligible list as one wave, mark all of it completed, and repeat. If an iteration produces no eligible nodes while unscheduled remains, pass the sorted unscheduled list to new DependencyCycleError and stop. Evaluate eligibility only against completed from prior iterations, ensuring all wave members depend only on earlier waves.
ordered_implementation_work: Inspect the existing graph input and preserve its object-key node universe and declared predecessor arrays without mutating either input collection.

Create a lexicographically sorted node list using the runtime's stable string comparison semantics (ordinary sort with the node names used by the existing API), and use it for every candidate scan and error list.
Initialize completed as an empty set, remaining as the full node-name set, and waves as an empty array.

For each iteration, derive eligible from the sorted remaining nodes by requiring every declared predecessor of each candidate to be present in completed; treat the entire iteration's completed set as the prior-wave state, not partially emitted candidates.
When eligible is nonempty, append it as the next wave, add all eligible nodes to completed, remove them from remaining, and continue.
When eligible is empty and remaining is nonempty, throw new DependencyCycleError([...remaining].sort(...)) so only nodes that could not be scheduled are reported and the list is deterministic.
Return waves after remaining becomes empty; preserve the existing empty-graph behavior implied by the algorithm as an empty wave list.

positive_non_ui: Run node --test through the project checker after implementation; all existing tests must pass without modification.
Confirm the fan-in case produces [["build","lint"],["package","test"],["audit"],["release"]].
Confirm equivalent graphs with reversed object keys and reversed dependency arrays produce the same [["a","b"],["c"]] result.
Confirm the cycle case throws an error whose name is DependencyCycleError, code is DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, and nodes is ["alpha","beta","gamma"] while free is absent from nodes.
Confirm no test files, package manifest, or dependencies changed and the implementation remains confined to src/waves.js.
